jurisdictions.name: Alaska

pay.text: Juror fees are set by the Alaska Court System (Administrative Rule 14); the court website could not be reached to confirm the amounts.

employer.text: Employers do not have to pay wages for time spent on jury service.

age.text: The jury statutes set no age-based exemption; exemptions are for health, family care, long-term disability or hardship.

term.text: No more than three months of jury service in any two-year period (a trial in progress must be finished).

frequency.text: A person who served as a juror in Alaska within the past year is disqualified from serving again.

deferral.text: Service can be deferred for hardship, temporary transportation problems or election work, to an agreed date no more than 10 months after the original date.

list: substantial hardship lasting more than two years
teacher at a designated low-performing school (during school term)
excuses.text: Claim the exemption with the court and show the reason.

penalty.text: Neglecting to attend when summoned is contempt of court; criminal contempt is a class A misdemeanor (up to 1 year and $25,000), civil contempt up to $5,000 per violation.

jurisdictions.unread: the Alaska Court System site (juror fees)

pay.mileage: A per-mile allowance for travel to and from court, amount set by the Alabama Supreme Court
pay.text: The statute leaves the daily expense allowance and mileage to an Alabama Supreme Court order or rule; the amount could not be confirmed on a reachable official page.

employer.text: Full-time employees keep their usual pay while on jury duty; employers cannot make them use vacation, sick or unpaid leave.
employer.notice: Employee must show the summons to the immediate supervisor on the next workday after receiving it.

age.text: Anyone 80 or older may ask in writing to be permanently exempt and removed from the jury list.

term.text: A selected juror serves for the length of the trial unless excused by the judge.

frequency.text: A person who served on a petit jury cannot be summoned again for 24 months; an excused juror is exempt for 24 months.

deferral.text: One automatic postponement on request (in person, phone, email or writing) to a fixed date within 6 months; a second only for an extreme emergency.

list: undue or extreme physical or financial hardship
sole caregiver with no substitute available
excuses.text: Apply to the court before the report date, with documentation if asked; being absent from work alone is not a hardship. An excused juror is exempt for 24 months.

penalty.text: Failing to obey a summons without good excuse is contempt of court: fine up to $300 and up to 10 days in county jail.

jurisdictions.name: Arkansas

pay.text: Set by the state and each county quorum court. Example (Clark County): $50 a day for jurors seated on a trial, $15 a day for those who report but are not selected (Mississippi County pays $30 to non-selected jurors). Statute not readable online, figures are county-reported.

employer.text: No wage obligation is stated by official court pages; the law protects the job, sick leave and vacation if the employee gives reasonable notice.
employer.notice: Employee must give the employer reasonable notice of the summons.

age.text: County circuit clerk pages state there is no age exemption in Arkansas beyond the minimum age of 18 (statute not verified).

term.text: County terms of several months (Clark County: three 4-month terms a year; Mississippi County: 2 months); jurors appear when called for trials during the term.

frequency.text: Not qualified if you served as a juror in the county in the last two years (county-reported qualification).

deferral.text: A 'deferment of term' lets you move your service to another term; it does not excuse you. Practice varies by county (Mississippi County allows no postponement).

list: excuse only by a judge (economic or business reasons not accepted)
excuses.text: Only a judge can excuse you; you may explain your situation to the judge in court.

missing: pay.law (Arkansas Code not readable on an official site; county-reported figures)
jurisdictions.unread: the Arkansas Code (published only through a commercial viewer) and the Arkansas Judiciary site
jurisdictions.caveat: What is shown for Arkansas comes from county circuit clerk pages (Clark and Pulaski counties), which report $50 a day for seated jurors and $15 for those not selected in Clark County; your county may differ.

pay.mileage: Round-trip mileage at the state employee rate (A.R.S. § 38-623); a juror excused on the first day gets mileage only
pay.text: Paid by the county. Superior court trial jurors who lose earnings can also ask the Fair Jury Improvement (lengthy trial) fund for $40 to $300 a day from day 1, if money is available.

employer.text: Employers need not pay wages, cannot force use of vacation or sick leave, and must restore the employee's position and seniority.

age.text: Anyone 75 or older may ask in writing to be excused, temporarily or permanently, and the court must grant it.

term.text: One day or one trial: service ends after one trial, or after one day without being assigned, or after the call-in period.

frequency.text: A juror selected to serve on a jury is not required to serve again for two years.

deferral.text: Two postponements on request (in person, phone, email or writing) to a date set by the jury commissioner; more only for an unforeseen extreme emergency.

list: mental or physical condition (medical statement required)
undue or extreme physical or financial hardship
sole caregiver with no substitute available
grand jury service within the last 4 years
temporary absence from the area or lack of transportation
excuses.text: Apply to the court before the report date with supporting documents (tax returns, payroll records, medical statement); missing work alone is not a hardship.

penalty.text: Wilfully missing jury service is unlawful: fine up to $500 and a new date; after a second summons the court may issue a body attachment as for contempt.

pay.mileage: At least 34 cents per mile to and from court from the second day, or up to $12 a day for public transit from the first day
pay.text: No fee on day 1. Government employees who keep full pay get no daily fee.

employer.text: Private employers are not required to pay wages during jury service, but must allow time off and may not fire or harass a juror.
employer.notice: The court advises telling the employer well in advance, as soon as the summons arrives.

age.text: No age exemption: advanced age is not a ground for exemption, though a serious health problem can lead to an excuse.

term.text: One day or one trial (statewide)

frequency.text: Not required to serve again for at least 12 months after reporting or serving

deferral.text: Follow the summons instructions (online or in writing) and give the earliest date you can serve; courts should grant a one-time deferral without requiring a court visit.

list: caregiver of a dependent who cannot be replaced
excuses.text: Request in writing on the summons response form with facts showing the hardship and why a deferral would not solve it; a doctor's note may be required.
excuses.law: Cal. Rules of Court, rule 2.1008; Code Civ. Proc. § 204

penalty.text: Fines from up to $250 for a first violation to $1,500 for three or more; possible contempt of court and incarceration.

jurisdictions.name: Colorado

pay.text: For the first 3 days the employer pays regular wages up to $50/day (self-employed may ask the court for up to $50/day; unemployed may claim certain expenses); from day 4 the state pays every juror $50/day.

employer.text: Employers must pay regular wages up to $50 per day for the first 3 days of service to regularly employed jurors (including part-time/temporary workers employed 3+ months).

age.text: Colorado grants no age-based exemption; only the 18+ minimum applies.

term.text: One day, or the length of one trial if impaneled (statewide).

frequency.text: Not qualified to serve if you served on a jury in any court within the past 12 months.

deferral.text: One postponement as of right: via the summons form (mail/email), the county's online postponement request, or the jury commissioner; generally to a date within 6 months (out-of-state students up to 12 months).

list: undue or extreme physical hardship (self or person under your care)
primary caregiver of a permanently disabled household member who does not work outside the home
physical or mental disability preventing service
served on a jury within the past 12 months
excuses.text: Submit the disqualification request with supporting documentation (e.g. a physician statement); students and military are not automatically excused but can postpone.

missing: penalty (C.R.S. 18-8-612 text not reachable on an official site)

jurisdictions.name: Connecticut

pay.mileage: 20 cents per mile round trip, counted within the out-of-pocket reimbursement for part-time/unemployed jurors during the first 5 days
pay.text: Days 1-5: full-time employees get regular wages from their employer; part-time and unemployed jurors are reimbursed out-of-pocket expenses ($20 to $50/day). From day 6, the state pays every juror $50/day.

employer.text: Employers must pay full-time employees (30+ hours/week) their regular wages for the first 5 days of jury service; no employer-size threshold.

age.text: People aged 75 or older may choose not to serve.

term.text: One day, or the length of the trial if impaneled.

frequency.text: Excused for 3 jury years after appearing for service (jury year runs Sept. 1 to Aug. 31).

deferral.text: Postpone online (Defer Your Jury Service page) to a date within 10 months of the original date; a second deferral or one within 2 weeks of the date requires calling Jury Administration (1-800-842-8175).

list: physical or mental disability (health care provider letter)
unable to speak and understand English
served within the 3 preceding jury years
federal jury service within 3 jury years
excuses.text: Request an excusal through the eResponse online portal, by email or by calling Jury Administration; students are expected to defer to a school break.

penalty.text: Failing to appear exposes the juror to a civil penalty whose amount is set by the Chief Court Administrator; the court may waive it. No jail term in the statute.

missing: penalty.maxFine (amount set administratively, not published in statute)

pay.mileage: No mileage; jurors still paid their salary get a $7 travel stipend per day
pay.text: The statute sets $30 a day plus up to $2 travel but lets the Board of Judges raise it; the court now pays $57 a day to jurors whose job does not pay them. Petit jurors who are summoned but do not serve on a jury are not paid the fee.

employer.text: Full-time employees working in DC are entitled to their usual pay (less the juror fee) for up to 5 days of service; employers with 10 or fewer employees are exempt.

age.text: People aged 70 or older may ask to be excused.

term.text: Petit jurors: one day unless picked for a trial (service ends for the day once panels are filled); grand jurors: 25 workdays.

frequency.text: Not required to serve again within 2 years

deferral.text: One postponement for any reason, via eJuror, email (jurorhelp@dcsc.gov), phone (202) 879-4604 or live chat.

list: caring for a child under 2.5 years
excuses.text: Ask through eJuror, by email or by phone to the Juror Office.
excuses.law: D.C. Code § 11-1909; D.C. Superior Court jury plan

penalty.text: A no-show who cannot show good cause may be held in contempt: up to $300 fine, 7 days in jail, or both.

jurisdictions.name: Delaware

pay.text: $20/day expense allowance (covers travel and parking). Under one-day/one-trial service (New Castle County) the first day is unpaid; in Kent and Sussex (two-week term) the $20 is paid for every day reported.

employer.text: No state law requires private employers to pay wages during jury service; the $20 allowance may not be treated as pay by the employer.

age.text: People over 70 may ask to be excused (send the questionnaire and a copy of a driver's license).

term.text: New Castle County: one day or one trial; Kent and Sussex Counties: a two-week term.

frequency.text: Not required to serve more than once every two years (Superior Court and federal court together).

deferral.text: Ask through the online qualification questionnaire or use 'Request Schedule Change' in the juror portal (one-time date change, not within 5 days of service; otherwise contact Jury Services). Out-of-state residents temporarily away for work or study are deferred until return.

list: served on a jury within the past two years
primary caregiver of persons unable to care for themselves
active full-time military or Delaware National Guard
self-employed or paid primarily on commission
excuses.text: Return the qualification questionnaire with a written request and supporting documents (doctor's note, employer letter, etc.) to the county Jury Services office.

penalty.text: Failing to appear and show cause is criminal contempt: up to $100 fine and/or up to 3 days in jail.

missing: pay.mileage (no separate mileage; included in $20 allowance)

jurisdictions.name: Florida

pay.text: Days 1-3: $15/day only for jurors who are not regularly employed or whose wages stop; employees who keep their wages get nothing from the clerk. From day 4 every juror gets $30/day. No separate travel reimbursement.

employer.text: No requirement for private employers to pay wages; jurors whose wages stop receive $15/day from the clerk for days 1-3.

age.text: Anyone 70 or older is excused on request, and may ask in writing to be permanently excused.

term.text: One day or one trial (statewide).

frequency.text: Anyone who reported as a prospective juror in their county within the past year is exempt for 1 year from the last day of service.

deferral.text: Service may be postponed up to 6 months on written or oral request to the clerk (up to 12 months during a declared emergency); you may propose a date.

list: hardship, extreme inconvenience or public necessity
parent not employed full time with custody of a child under 6
gave birth within the 6 months before the reporting date
caregiver of a person incapable of caring for themselves
permanent physical or mental incapacity (physician statement)
reported for jury service within the past year
excuses.text: Ask the clerk of court in the county that summoned you; most statutory excusals are granted on request, others at the judge's discretion.

penalty.text: Failing to attend without sufficient excuse: fine up to $100, and it may also be treated as contempt of court.

missing: penalty.maxJailDays (contempt, no fixed cap in ch. 40)
portal (no statewide juror page found on flcourts.gov)

jurisdictions.name: Georgia

pay.text: Each county sets a daily expense allowance between $5 and $50 (most pay about $25), paid from the first day including jury selection.

employer.text: Employers must give time off for jury duty, but it may be unpaid.

age.text: People 70 or older may claim an exemption (and can sign an affidavit to be removed from the jury list permanently); contact the court before the appearance date.

term.text: Set by each county: if not selected you are released and the summons is complete; some counties summon for a week (e.g. Fayette County).

frequency.text: Not eligible if you served on a jury in the last 12 months.

deferral.text: Handled by the county clerk of superior court; e.g. Fayette County grants a one-time deferral via the notarized affidavit on the back of the summons, with documentation.

list: active military service member or spouse
primary teacher in a home study program
primary caregiver of a child age 6 or younger
primary unpaid caregiver of a person unable to care for themselves
permanent mental or physical disability (doctor's affidavit)
not a resident of the county
served on a jury in the last 12 months
excuses.text: Contact the court before your appearance date; counties use a notarized affidavit for exemption with supporting documents.

penalty.text: Failing to respond may lead to a fine or other penalties (contempt of court); no statewide amount found on an official page.

missing: Georgia Code text not readable on an official site (Lexis-hosted); figures taken from georgia.gov and Fayette County clerk
jurisdictions.caveat: Georgia sets most jury procedures county by county. Term, postponement and excuses below come from one county clerk (Fayette County); your county may differ.

pay.mileage: 33 cents per mile, round trip from home to court
pay.text: Raised from $30 to $50 a day on July 1, 2026 (first increase since 1989). Jurors excused at their own request may get mileage only.

employer.text: No Hawaii law requires employers to pay wages during jury service; some do voluntarily or under union contracts.

age.text: People aged 80 or older may claim an optional exemption on the juror questionnaire.

term.text: Selection usually takes one day; if chosen you serve for the whole trial, often three to four days.

deferral.text: Write to or call the court explaining the conflict (written request required in the 2nd, 3rd and 5th circuits); only one deferral per summons.

list: active military deployed out of state
police, fire or emergency medical services personnel
living more than 70 miles from the court
breastfeeding a child aged two or under
disability or medical condition (with physician certificate)
excuses.text: Optional exemptions are claimed on the questionnaire. Other excuse requests must be in writing, signed, with supporting documents, and sent at least two weeks before the appearance date.

pay.mileage: Round-trip mileage at the rate set by the Iowa Supreme Court, plus actual parking costs
pay.text: Statute sets $30 a day and lets the Supreme Court add pay after 7 days; the Judicial Branch pays $50 a day from day 8.

employer.text: No Iowa law requires employers to pay wages during jury service.
employer.notice: Court advises telling the employer well in advance, ideally on receipt of the summons (not a statutory condition).

age.text: No age-based exemption; older jurors need a medical, disability or other good-cause reason.

term.text: Set by each county court, up to 3 months, longer only to finish a case.

frequency.text: Excused if you served as a state grand or trial juror within the past two years.

deferral.text: Postpone up to 12 months online or by phone at least 10 days before the reporting date; the first request is granted automatically.

list: sole caregiver of a person with a permanent disability at home (not employed outside home)
breastfeeding mother caring for the child (not employed outside home)
served as a state juror within the past two years
excuses.text: Send written proof with the questionnaire; caregiving and breastfeeding excuses do not apply if you work outside the home.

penalty.text: Failing to appear without sufficient cause can be punished as contempt; before a district judge, up to $500 and/or 6 months in jail.

jurisdictions.name: Idaho

pay.mileage: Mileage from home to the courthouse at the county employee rate
pay.text: State law sets a floor of $5 per half day or $10 per full day; counties pay more (e.g. Bingham County pays $25 per half day and $50 per full day).

employer.text: Paying wages during jury service is not required; it is up to the employer (county court guidance).

age.text: People 70 or older may ask to be excused by marking the jury qualification form (county court guidance).

term.text: Varies by court; in Bingham County a panel term lasts four months.

frequency.text: In Bingham County, after a full panel term you may ask not to serve again for two years (county practice).

deferral.text: Follow the instructions on the summons, which vary by court; contact the court's jury commissioner.

list: temporary or chronic medical condition (physician's letter)
excuses.text: No automatic exemptions; requests go to the county jury commissioner with documentation. Grounds listed come from the Idaho Supreme Court page and Bingham County's court FAQ.

missing: pay.law, employer.law, age.law, excuses.law (legislature.idaho.gov unreachable: connection refused)
jurisdictions.caveat: Several rules below come from one county court page (Bingham County) because the state code site could not be reached; your county may differ.

jurisdictions.name: Illinois

pay.text: Juror fees are paid by each county; figure shown is Cook County (Circuit Court of Cook County). The statewide statute (55 ILCS 5/4-11001) could not be read because ilga.gov was unreachable.

employer.text: Employers are not required to pay wages during jury service.

age.text: Cook County runs a Senior Citizen Opt-Out Program: people 70 or older can call before their date to decline or transfer. Not a statewide statutory exemption as far as verified.

term.text: Cook County: one day or one trial. Practice in other counties not verified.

frequency.text: Cook County: not called again for 12 months after serving.

deferral.text: Cook County: call (312) 603-JURY; the date can be pushed back 11 or 22 weeks (e.g. vacation, student or teacher during school, seasonal work).

list: nursing mother (excused on request by statute)
living in a nursing home or institution
excuses.text: Cook County requires documentation for each excuse; nursing mothers are excused on request under 705 ILCS 305/10.3.

penalty.text: Not appearing can lead to contempt of court and a fine or other penalty (Cook County guidance); statutory maximum not verified.

missing: statewide statutory pay minimum and pay.law (ilga.gov / lrb.ilga.gov unreachable: connection refused)
jurisdictions.unread: the Illinois General Assembly site (statewide juror fee)
jurisdictions.caveat: Term, postponement and the age rule below come from the Circuit Court of Cook County, where the Cook County fee is $35 a day; other counties set their own fee and may differ.

jurisdictions.name: Indiana

pay.mileage: State-employee mileage rate for each mile traveled to and from court (counties may pay parking instead)
pay.text: Circuit/superior courts: $30 a day until the jury is impaneled, then $80 a day through the 5th day of trial and $90 a day from the 6th trial day (day counts refer to trial days). Counties may add a supplemental fee. City/town courts pay $15 a day.

employer.text: No wage-continuation duty; employers cannot force employees to use annual, vacation or sick leave for jury service.
employer.notice: Employee must notify the employer within a reasonable period after receiving the summons and before appearing.

age.text: People 75 or older may be exempted by notifying the jury administrator.

term.text: One trial: you serve until the end of the first trial you are sworn for; if not selected, service ends when jury selection is complete.

frequency.text: Cannot serve again as a trial juror in the same county within 365 days of a case that reached a verdict; after serving you are not recalled until the whole pool has been called.

deferral.text: One deferral as of right for hardship, extreme inconvenience or necessity: contact the jury administrator by phone, email, letter or in person and pick a new date within one year.

list: gave birth in the past 365 days and currently breastfeeding
physical or mental disability (physician certificate may be required)
employer with 10 or fewer employees already has a worker on jury service (rescheduling)
excuses.text: Notify the jury administrator; facts supporting an exemption are recorded under oath.

penalty.text: Failing to appear or complete service is criminal contempt; the statute sets no specific maximum. Lying on the qualification form is a Class C misdemeanor.

missing: portal (no statewide juror page found on in.gov/courts)

pay.mileage: Mileage at the rate authorized by law, for travel to and from court
pay.text: Each county commission sets the daily fee between $10 and $50; $10 is the statutory minimum.

employer.text: No Kansas statute requires private employers to keep paying wages; the law only bars firing permanent employees for jury service.

age.text: Kansas law lists no age-based exemption; an older person can only be excused for physical or mental infirmity or hardship.

term.text: Set by each district court; e.g. Sedgwick County (Wichita) calls panels for one week, or until the trial ends if selected.

frequency.text: Excused if you served as a juror in the same county within the preceding year.

deferral.text: Call the county jury clerk before the summons date; Sedgwick County allows one rescheduling for temporary extraordinary or compelling hardship.

list: presence elsewhere required for public welfare, health or safety
served as a juror in the county within the past year
excuses.text: Ask the court (the jury clerk) to be excused; send supporting documents such as a doctor's note.

penalty.text: Fine of up to $100 for each day of unexcused absence; may also be held in contempt.

pay.text: $5 per day for service plus $7.50 per day expense reimbursement ($12.50 total), paid for every day you attend even if not seated.

employer.text: No statute requires wages during service; employers may not fire, threaten or coerce an employee over jury service (Class B misdemeanor under KRS 29A.990).

age.text: People 70 or older can ask, on the juror qualification form, to be excused for the period summoned.

term.text: No more than 30 court days of petit jury service in any 24-month period, unless needed to finish a case.

frequency.text: Service limits are counted over a 24-month period (30 court days, one grand jury, not both grand and petit).

deferral.text: Ask the Chief Circuit Judge or a designated clerk/administrator; staff can postpone up to 12 months, a judge up to 24 months.

excuses.text: Request an excuse before or on the day you are summoned; judges favour postponement or reduced service over a permanent excuse.

penalty.text: A no-show is ordered to appear and show cause, and may be punished for contempt; the statute sets no specific amount.

pay.mileage: Mileage at the state-officials rate per mile to and from the courthouse (one charge each way)
pay.text: $25 a day is the statutory pay for jurors in criminal cases, paid by the parish; civil-jury pay is set separately by court and can differ.

employer.text: Employers must grant up to one day of paid jury leave (no loss of wages or leave); beyond that, pay is not required. Firing for jury service is banned, with fines of $100 to $1,000 per employee.
employer.notice: Employee must notify the employer within a reasonable time after receiving the summons and before appearing.

age.text: People 70 or older are exempt under the state constitution and may decline to serve, or choose to serve.

frequency.text: Anyone who served on a jury in the last two years may claim an exemption (as stated by the 21st Judicial District Court).

deferral.text: Contact the parish clerk of court before your date; one postponement, to a date within six months (21st Judicial District practice; parishes set their own procedure).

list: served on a jury within the last two years
mental or physical condition (physician documentation, up to 24 months)
undue or extreme physical or financial hardship (caring for a dependent, daily living costs, illness)
excuses.text: Apply to the judge with documents (tax returns, doctor's statements, proof of dependency) before your appearance date; missing work alone is not hardship.
excuses.law: La. R.S. 13:3042 (noted as superseded by La. Supreme Court Rule XXV); La. Const. art. V, §33

penalty.text: The district judge can fine a no-show up to $50 and/or jail up to 3 days per violation.

jurisdictions.name: Massachusetts

pay.text: Days 1-3 are paid by the employer (regular wages); from day 4 the state pays $50 a day, with no extra travel reimbursement. Unemployed, retired and other non-employed jurors can get up to $50 a day of expenses for days 1-3.

employer.text: Every employer must pay regular wages for the first 3 days (including part-time, temporary and casual staff); a court can excuse an employer for extreme financial hardship, in which case the state pays up to $50 a day.

age.text: People 70 or older can opt out by saying so on the summons response.

term.text: One day or one trial (statewide); grand jurors serve three months.

frequency.text: Disqualified if you served on a state or federal jury in the previous 3 years.

deferral.text: One postponement as of right, for up to one year, chosen on the summons response; further deferrals only for hardship, inconvenience or public necessity.

list: extreme hardship (decided strictly by the court)
sole daily caregiver of a permanently disabled household member (physician letter)
moved out of the judicial district
not able to speak and understand English
excuses.text: Disqualifications are claimed on the summons response with the required letters; a full excuse from trial service needs a court finding of extreme hardship.

penalty.text: Failing to appear is a crime punishable by a fine of up to $2,000; the court may also issue an arrest warrant. No jail term is set by the statute.

jurisdictions.caveat: Some texts cited on this page were read in archived copies (web.archive.org, 2025 and 2026) of the official pages linked, because the official site refused our connection on October 29, 2026.

pay.text: State per diem of $30 a day, plus any county supplement (total generally $30-$40); a trial juror gets $50 from the 6th day of one trial.

employer.text: No wage requirement, but employers cannot make you use annual, sick or vacation leave for jury service, and cannot require a shift starting after 5 p.m. (or before 3 a.m. next day) after 4+ hours of service.

age.text: People 70 or older are exempt if they ask the jury commissioner in writing.

term.text: Length of service is set by each circuit court's jury plan; ask your local jury office.

frequency.text: Not required to serve more than once in any 3-year period, unless a county jury plan provides otherwise (e.g. after 1 year if you served under 5 days).

deferral.text: One-time change of report date online in participating counties, otherwise contact the local jury office with a pressing reason.

list: sole caregiver of a child under 3
excuses.text: Show the reason on the questionnaire, in an interview or with other evidence; excuses last only as long as needed and are limited to two unless extraordinary.

penalty.text: Failing to appear: up to $1,000 and/or 60 days in jail (90 days for not completing service; 30 days for not returning the qualification form).

pay.mileage: Mileage from home to court and back at the state rate set in 5 M.R.S. § 8
pay.text: $15 for each day you are required to attend, plus mileage.

employer.text: No statute requires wages; employers may not fire, threaten or cut health insurance because of jury service (Class E crime; lost wages recoverable up to 6 weeks).

age.text: Anyone 80 or older who does not wish to serve is excused on request.

term.text: The usual call is 15 court days (longer only to finish a case); in practice most jurors serve one day of selection.

frequency.text: No more than once in any 5-year period and no more than 3 times in a lifetime as a trial juror.

deferral.text: Contact the court clerk before your date to ask to postpone; the court must approve and may reschedule to a less burdensome season.

list: physical or mental disability (physician certificate may be required)
excuses.text: Ask the clerk with written documentation (a medical note for health reasons); self-employment alone is not an excuse.

penalty.text: Contempt: up to $100 fine and/or up to 3 days in jail after a show-cause hearing.

pay.mileage: At least 20 cents per mile
pay.text: Statutory minimums since April 1, 2018: $30 a full day ($15 a half day) for the first day, then $45 ($22.50 half day). Counties may pay more with county board approval.

employer.text: Employers must release the employee but are not required to keep paying wages.

age.text: People over 70 may claim an exemption if they request it.

term.text: Set by each court; state law allows but does not require one day/one trial, and the state best-practice manual recommends no more than two weeks.

frequency.text: Not qualified if you served as a juror within the past 12 months.

deferral.text: Handled by each court's jury clerk; contact the clerk as soon as possible (example: the 15th District Court grants only one postponement). Students' service is postponed to the end of the school or academic year.

excuses.text: Exemptions must be requested; other excusals are at the court's discretion, and job reasons are generally not accepted.

penalty.text: Failing to attend court when summoned is punishable as contempt of court (MCL 600.1346); contempt is capped at a $7,500 fine and 93 days in jail (MCL 600.1715).

pay.mileage: 54 cents per mile, round trip from home to the courthouse
pay.text: Rates are set statewide by the Judicial Branch (statute delegates to the supreme court); paid only for days you must report. Child care and parking can be reimbursed, parking is deducted from the daily rate.

employer.text: No wage obligation, but the employer must release the employee and may not force an alternative shift on reporting days.

age.text: Anyone 70 or older who asks to be excused is excused automatically, with no proof needed.

term.text: Term set by county size: 2 weeks in counties of 100,000+, up to 2 months (50,000-100,000), up to 4 months (50,000 or less); service ends after 10 days actually reported.

frequency.text: Not qualified to serve again within 4 years of state or federal jury service (2 years if the county runs short of jurors).

deferral.text: Ask the jury commissioner; deferral is for a reasonable time set by the county jury plan and is preferred to an excuse.

list: continuing hardship to the juror or the public
impaired ability to receive and evaluate information (excused by a judge)
legislators and legislative staff during session (deferral)
excuses.text: Request an excuse from the jury commissioner; automatic excuses are abolished except those in Rule 808.

penalty.text: Failing to appear without good cause is a misdemeanor (up to $1,000 fine and/or 90 days in jail under the general misdemeanor penalty, Minn. Stat. § 609.03).

pay.mileage: State-employee mileage rate (RSMo 33.095), round trip from home to the courthouse
pay.text: Statutory floor is $6 a day plus mileage; counties may add more (at least $18 total if the county adds $6, with $6 reimbursed by the state). A county may instead opt for $50 a day from the third day, with nothing for the first two days.

employer.text: No statute requires wages; an employer may not require or request that the employee use vacation, sick or personal leave for jury service.

age.text: People aged 75 or older are excused if they apply to the court in time.

frequency.text: Anyone who served on a state or federal jury in the preceding two years is excused on timely application.

deferral.text: One postponement as of right: ask the board of jury commissioners in person, by phone, email or in writing; the new date is within 6 months (12 for full-time students). A second postponement only for an unforeseeable extreme emergency.

list: served on a jury in the preceding two years
absence from work would harm public safety, health or welfare
undue or extreme physical or financial hardship (e.g. no substitute caregiver, costs threatening daily living expenses, risk of illness)
health care provider whose absence would harm patients
religious institution employee whose obligations forbid jury service
excuses.text: Apply to the court before the reporting date; hardship excuses are decided by a judge and need a ruling by the date you are due to appear.

penalty.text: Willful no-show is civil contempt: after a show-cause hearing the court may fine up to $500 and/or order community service. The statute sets no jail term.

jurisdictions.name: Mississippi

pay.mileage: Mileage at the rate authorized by Miss. Code § 25-3-41
pay.text: Each county board of supervisors sets the daily fee between $25 and $40 (circuit, chancery, county courts; justice court $10-$15). Bills to raise the cap died in 2024 and 2025. A Lengthy Trial Fund can top up wages in civil trials over 10 days. Official code text read via legislature bill reproductions (the code itself is hosted by Lexis).

employer.text: No wage obligation in the statute; an employer may not require or request that the employee use annual, vacation or sick leave for jury service.
employer.notice: Employee must tell the employer of the summons within a reasonable time after receiving it to be protected.
employer.law: Miss. Code § 13-5-35 (enacted as § 15 of H.B. 13, 2004 1st Ex. Sess.)

age.text: Anyone over 65 is exempt if they claim it; the claim can be made to the circuit clerk outside court.

frequency.text: Anyone who served on a grand jury or on a trial jury in a litigated case within the last 2 years may claim an exemption.

deferral.text: One postponement as of right (if none in the past 2 years): contact the circuit clerk in person, by phone, email or in writing and fix a new date within 6 months or two court terms. A second postponement only for an unforeseeable extreme emergency.

list: illness making the juror incapable of service (physician certificate to the clerk)
undue or extreme physical or financial hardship (no substitute caregiver, costs threatening daily living expenses, physical hardship)
served on a jury within 2 years (on request)
Mississippi National Guard on active duty (superior officer statement)
excuses.text: Illness excuses can go to the clerk with a doctor's certificate; hardship excuses are decided by a judge, need documents (tax returns, medical statements...) and must be ruled on before the reporting date. Being away from work alone is not a hardship.

penalty.text: A no-show without good cause is in civil contempt: up to $500 fine, up to 3 days in jail, or both; the court may also order community service.

jurisdictions.caveat: The Mississippi Code is published online only by a commercial service. The rules on this page were read in bills on the Legislature's own site that reproduce the code sections in force when they were filed; a later amendment may not be reflected.

jurisdictions.name: Montana

pay.mileage: Mileage allowance under MCA 2-18-503, each way between home and court
pay.text: Panel members get $12 a day; jurors selected for a case get an additional $13 a day ($25 total) while serving. A juror excused at their own request on the first day forfeits per diem and mileage.

employer.notice: Employee must give the employer reasonable notice of the summons

age.text: Anyone 75 or older who asks must be excused by the court or jury commissioner.

term.text: Counties draw jurors for a jury term (e.g. Lewis and Clark County: a one-year term, September to August); after serving on a trial you are not called again for about two months.

deferral.text: Ask the Clerk of District Court to be made unavailable for set dates (e.g. vacation, doctor appointment) before being drawn for a specific trial.

list: undue hardship (for you, a dependent or the public you serve)
personal care of a sick, aged or special-needs dependent
chronic incapacity from illness or injury (permanent exclusion, with physician certification)
excuses.text: Send an affidavit stating the facts to the jury commissioner; the court decides. Chronically incapacitated people can ask for permanent exclusion with a physician's certificate.

penalty.text: A summoned juror who willfully fails to attend may be attached (brought in) and fined up to $50; the statute sets no jail term.

missing: employer.law (no statute located; protection stated by county clerk page)

jurisdictions.name: North Carolina

pay.mileage: Only for jurors summoned from outside the county to a special venire, at the State employee rate
pay.text: Uniform statewide fees: $12 for day 1, $20 a day after, and $40 a day for each day beyond 5 days served in any 24-month period. Grand jurors get $20 a day.

employer.text: No statute requires employers to keep paying wages; the law only forbids firing or demoting an employee for jury service.

age.text: People 72 or older may ask to be excused, deferred or exempted by filing a signed statement, without appearing, at least 5 business days before the report date.

term.text: One week: jurors serve for the week summoned and are discharged at the end of the weekly session, unless sitting on a trial, which they must finish.

frequency.text: A person who served as a juror in the preceding two years is not qualified, so cannot be required to serve again within 2 years (6 years after a full grand jury term).

deferral.text: Requests to be excused or deferred go to the chief district court judge (or the clerk or staff designated) under procedures set in each district; jurors 72+, full-time students and people with a disability may file a signed statement without appearing, at least 5 business days before the report date. Deferred jurors are added to a later session.

list: service contrary to public welfare, health or safety
full-time student at an out-of-state college (classes or exams)
excuses.text: Excuses are granted only for compelling personal hardship or public welfare, health or safety, on the form from the Administrative Office of the Courts, decided by the chief district court judge or a delegate before the session. A judge may require an excused juror to serve at a later session.

penalty.text: A summoned juror who fails to appear without a sufficient excuse can be fined up to $50, entered as a judgment if unpaid. The statute sets no jail term.

missing: deferral: no statewide online postponement procedure read (nccourts.gov unreachable)

pay.mileage: State-employee mileage rate (N.D.C.C. 54-06-09)
pay.text: $100 per day of required attendance in district court, paid by the state; only $50 for the first day if attendance that day is four hours or less.

employer.text: The jury chapter imposes no duty on employers to pay wages; it only protects the job.

age.text: No age exemption: the statute says no qualified juror is exempt; older jurors can only ask to be excused for undue hardship.

term.text: No more than ten court days as a trial juror in any two-year period, unless needed to finish a case.

frequency.text: Service is capped at ten court days and one grand jury per two-year period; no separate waiting period is set.

deferral.text: The court may excuse a juror for a period it deems necessary, after which the juror must report again (a postponement).

excuses.text: Ask the court on the qualification form or by interview; the excuse is temporary and the court sets when you report again.

penalty.text: The jury chapter's penalty section for failing to serve (§ 27-09.1-16) was repealed in 1993; no specific penalty for not appearing is set in the chapter.

jurisdictions.name: Nebraska

pay.mileage: Mileage paid in addition (rate not stated on the court page)
pay.text: $35 for each day of required service plus mileage; checks are mailed by the county clerk 2 to 4 weeks after service.
pay.law: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 25-1640 (per court forms; statute site unreachable)

employer.text: Employers may not dock pay for jury service; they may only reduce wages by the $35/day juror fee (expense reimbursements excluded). Applies to all employers.
employer.notice: Employee must give reasonable notice of the summons; shift workers must be excused from shift work on request

age.text: People 70 or older can be exempted by sending a written request.

term.text: Depends on the court: from one day to several weeks; you may have to check in daily.

frequency.text: Not required to serve if, in the past 5 years, you served more than 4 weeks as a petit juror, on more than one grand jury, or on both a grand and a petit jury.

deferral.text: Written request to the judge (form DC 8:4, Application for Postponement of Jury Service) showing undue hardship, extreme inconvenience or public necessity; granted for a limited period.

excuses.text: Notify the clerk of the court that summoned you in writing immediately; a judge reviews the request.

penalty.text: Failing to respond to a summons without good cause, or to answer the qualification form, can lead to contempt of court. (Employers who violate § 25-1674 commit a Class IV misdemeanor.)

missing: oneDayOneTrial (nebraskalegislature.gov unreachable from this environment; statutes not read)

jurisdictions.name: New Hampshire

pay.mileage: 20 cents per mile round trip, only if you live outside the town or city of the courthouse
pay.text: $10 per half day, $20 per full day, paid by the state; State of NH employees get mileage only.

employer.text: No NH statute read requires wages during jury service; RSA 500-A:14 protects the job only. Fired employees can sue within 1 year for lost wages and reinstatement.

age.text: People 70 or older may ask to be excused through eResponse if they do not wish to serve (eligibility is set by court rule under RSA 500-A:5).
age.law: RSA 500-A:5 (eligibility by rule of court); NH Judicial Branch jurors page

term.text: Petit jurors are summoned for a month and may sit on several trials; no more than 30 days (six 5-day weeks) unless on an ongoing trial. Grand jurors usually serve 1 to 3 days a month.

frequency.text: People who actually attended court as jurors are not put back on the master list for at least 3 years.

deferral.text: Ask through the eResponse questionnaire to defer to another month (e.g. out-of-state student, legislator in session, pending case, temporary medical condition, hardship); a judge rules on it.

list: served in NH Superior Court in the last 3 years
excuses.text: Request an excusal or deferral in eResponse; a judge decides. The statute allows excuse for undue hardship, extreme inconvenience, public necessity or other cause the court finds appropriate (RSA 500-A:11).

penalty.text: Failing to appear and to show cause is a misdemeanor (RSA 500-A:20). An unclassified misdemeanor is presumed class B (fine up to $1,200, no jail) unless the state seeks class A penalties (up to 1 year and $2,000) under RSA 625:9 IV(c) and 651:2.

jurisdictions.name: New Jersey

pay.text: Petit jurors get $5 a day for the first 3 days and $40 a day from day 4; grand and State grand jurors get $5 a day. Full-time State employees get no juror fee but keep their regular wages (N.J.S.A. 2B:20-16).

employer.text: No statute requires private employers to pay wages during jury service; State agencies keep paying their full-time employees.

age.text: People 75 or older may ask to be excused by giving their date of birth to the Jury Management Office, either for the upcoming date only or permanently.

frequency.text: Anyone who served in the same county within the last 3 years may ask to be excused; this is not automatic, and federal service does not count.

deferral.text: After completing the qualification questionnaire, a juror may defer (reschedule) once through the My Jury Service Portal or by contacting the county Jury Management Office, choosing a new date and a reason (medical, transportation, travel, student, emergency, employment).

list: served in the same county within 3 years
medical condition unlikely to change within a year
sole care of a minor child or of a sick, aged or infirm dependent
nursing or expressing milk for a child one year or younger
provider of highly specialized healthcare services who cannot be replaced
healthcare worker essential to a disabled person's care
active volunteer firefighter or rescue squad member
excuses.text: Complete the qualification questionnaire first, then mail or email the required documents (certification, doctor's form, employer or superintendent letter, orders) to the county Jury Management Office.

penalty.text: The court site says only that failing to respond to the summons leads to further court action; no fine or jail figure was read in an official source.

pay.mileage: $0.70 per mile, round trip, for mileage over 40 miles
pay.text: New Mexico pays jurors by the hour, not by the day: $12.00 per hour, set by New Mexico Supreme Court order.

employer.text: No duty to pay wages; but an employer may not make an employee use annual, vacation or sick leave for jury service. A violation is a petty misdemeanor.

age.text: People 75 or older may ask the court for a permanent exemption (one request each to the district and magistrate court of their county).

term.text: Set by each court; the summons or local jury office gives the length.

frequency.text: Generally not required to serve in a New Mexico state court more than once every 3 years (proof of actual service needed).

deferral.text: One postponement can be requested through the online Jury Questionnaire; a second is allowed only for an unforeseen extreme emergency. You must appear unless told it was granted.

list: medical condition or disability (with healthcare provider statement)
excuses.text: Excusal is granted only in very limited circumstances, in writing with documents; a medical excuse needs a signed statement from a healthcare provider. Moral or religious beliefs are not a ground.

penalty.text: Willfully failing to appear can be punished under NMSA § 38-5-10; failure to appear and contempt are criminal charges that can bring jail, a fine or both.

jurisdictions.name: Nevada

pay.mileage: 36.5 cents a mile if you live 30 miles or more (one way) from the place of trial
pay.text: $65 a day from the third day of jury selection, or from the day you are sworn in as a juror if earlier; the first two days of selection are unpaid unless you are sworn.

employer.text: NRS 6.190 does not require wages, but an employer may not force you to use sick leave or vacation time, nor make you work within 8 hours before reporting (or that evening after 4+ hours of service).
employer.notice: Give the employer notice (sent with the summons) at least 3 days before reporting

age.text: People 70 or over may ask to be excused from all jury service (affidavit); 65+ living 65 miles or more from the court may also ask.

term.text: Clark County (Eighth Judicial District): if not assigned to a panel or selected the first day, service is complete; sworn jurors serve for the trial (average 3 to 5 days).

frequency.text: Clark County: not called again for at least 18 months (federal court may still summon you).

deferral.text: Clark County: request a deferral through the online jury questionnaire, then email supporting documents to jury@clarkcountycourts.us.

list: serious illness or death in immediate family
primary caregiver of a person needing constant assistance
excuses.text: Ask through the court's jury questionnaire with documentation; the court may excuse temporarily on these grounds and must permanently excuse people with a disabling permanent condition (doctor's certificate may be required).

penalty.text: A no-show is ordered to show cause; without good cause it is contempt with a fine of up to $500 (no jail term in NRS 6.040).

pay.text: $72 per day of attendance in state courts (amended 2025). Employed jurors whose employer must keep paying at least $72 do not also get the state fee; if wages are under $72 the state pays the difference.

employer.text: Employers with more than 10 employees may not withhold the first $72 of daily wages for the first 3 days of jury service; after that, pay may be withheld.
employer.notice: Employee must notify the employer before the term of service begins

age.text: The qualifications set only a minimum age of 18; the statute sets no upper age limit and no age exemption.

term.text: Trial jurors serve no more than five court days of actual attendance (or less if the commissioner sets it), but stay until any trial they are on ends.

frequency.text: Not eligible to serve again in state courts for 6 years after the last day of service (8 years if service lasted more than 10 days).

deferral.text: One postponement to a definite date when court is in session, no more than 6 months after the original date; a breastfeeding mother may postpone up to 2 years. Ask the county commissioner of jurors.

list: hardship to a person under the juror's care
excuses.text: Apply to the commissioner of jurors or the court; excusal requires incapacity, or undue hardship or extreme inconvenience to you, a person in your care, or the public.

penalty.text: Civil penalty of up to $250 for failing to return the questionnaire or to appear; the section sets no jail term (ignoring a court order can bring other penalties).

jurisdictions.name: Ohio

pay.text: No statewide figure: each board of county commissioners sets the daily rate. After 10 days of actual service, pay rises to the greater of $15 or 1.5 times the county rate (the county may go up to 2 times).

employer.text: Ohio law does not require wages during jury service; employers may not require or request use of vacation, sick or annual leave.
employer.notice: Employee must give the employer reasonable notice of the summons before service starts.

age.text: A juror over 75 is excused if they ask, by telling the court's jury employee in person, by phone, in writing or by email before the reporting date.

term.text: A juror who has actually served two consecutive calendar weeks is discharged (unless a trial is still under way).

frequency.text: After such a discharge, no jury service in any Ohio court until the second jury year after the last service (counties under 100,000 people set their own rule).

deferral.text: One postponement is granted automatically if asked at least two business days before the first appearance (phone, writing or email) and a new date within six months is agreed; further postponements only for extreme emergencies. Small employers (25 or fewer staff) get an automatic postponement if another employee served in the prior 30 days.

list: public interest materially injured by attendance
recent death or dangerous illness of spouse or near relative
cloistered member of a religious order
mental or physical condition (documentation may be required)
undue or extreme physical or financial hardship
breastfeeding a baby one year old or younger
active member of an Amish sect
excuses.text: Ask the court or jury commissioners before the reporting date, with documentation for hardship. Missing work alone is not a hardship. Excuses last only for that jury year unless the grounds are permanent.

penalty.text: Failing to attend violates § 2313.20 and is punished as contempt: first offense up to $250 and 30 days in jail; second up to $500 and 60 days; third or later up to $1,000 and 90 days.

jurisdictions.name: Oklahoma

pay.mileage: Daily round-trip mileage under the State Travel Reimbursement Act; parking may be provided
pay.text: $50 per day of attendance. For trials longer than 10 days, the Lengthy Trial Fund may add wage replacement of up to $200 a day from day 11 (and up to $50 a day for days 4-10 on proven hardship).

employer.text: Employers need not pay wages unless the employee chooses to use paid leave; they cannot require or request use of leave. Firing or adverse action is a misdemeanor (fine up to $5,000).
employer.notice: Employee must notify the employer within a reasonable time after receiving the summons and before reporting.

age.text: People over 70 cannot be compelled to serve; they may decline.

term.text: One day per calendar year, unless selected (or under consideration) for a trial; then for the length of the trial.

frequency.text: Anyone who served as a grand or trial juror in the five preceding calendar years cannot be compelled to serve again.

deferral.text: One postponement as of right: ask the court clerk in person, by phone, email or in writing and fix a new date within six months. A second only for an extreme emergency. Automatic postponement if a co-worker at an employer with 5 or fewer full-time staff was summoned for the same period.

list: served in the last five calendar years (not compelled)
mental or physical condition (medical documentation required)
undue or extreme physical or financial hardship
excuses.text: Ask the judge before the reporting date with documents (tax returns, medical statements, proof of dependency). Missing work alone is not a hardship. A non-permanent excuse lasts two years.

missing: penalty (no juror-specific no-show penalty found in Title 38; OSCN unreachable from our network)

jurisdictions.name: Oregon

pay.mileage: 20 cents per mile round trip for circuit court (public transit tickets reimbursed instead, any distance)
pay.text: Circuit court: $10 a day for days 1-2, then $25 a day from day 3. Jurors whose employer keeps paying them must waive the fee unless their employment agreement says otherwise.

employer.text: No Oregon law requires wages during jury service; employers cannot force use of paid leave and must allow unpaid leave. Employers with 10+ employees must keep insurance if the employee elects it.
employer.notice: To keep insurance coverage, the employee must notify the employer under its notification policy.

age.text: Anyone 70 or older is excused on request (by phone, mail or the court's method), but must still respond to the summons.

term.text: One day or one trial is the statutory goal for circuit courts; term length is set locally, but no trial juror serves more than 10 days unless needed to finish a trial.

frequency.text: Not eligible if you served as a juror in an Oregon state or federal court within the last 24 months.

deferral.text: Request a postponement in the county's online eResponse portal after completing the qualification form. One deferral for good cause, to a term starting within a year; more only for good cause with 10 available dates in the next six months.

list: undue hardship or extreme inconvenience (to you, your family, employer or the public)
sole caregiver of a child or dependent who cannot afford other care
excuses.text: Ask through the county eResponse portal (or phone/mail); the court reviews each request. No permanent excusal is required by law.

penalty.text: A no-show is ordered to show cause and can be held in contempt; punitive contempt allows a fine of up to $500 or 1% of annual gross income (whichever is greater) and up to six months in jail.

jurisdictions.name: Pennsylvania

pay.mileage: 17 cents per mile, round trip (none in Philadelphia, the first judicial district)
pay.text: $9 a day for the first three days of service in a calendar year, then $25 a day for each later day that year.

employer.text: No duty to pay wages; firing or penalising a juror is a summary offense. Protection does not cover retail/service employers with fewer than 15 staff or manufacturers with fewer than 40 (those employees may ask to be excused).

age.text: People aged 75 or older are excused if they ask.

term.text: Set by each county. Many counties (e.g. Lehigh) use one day or one trial.

frequency.text: Exempt for 3 years after serving on a jury; only 1 year if you served fewer than 3 days that year.

deferral.text: Postponements are handled by each county's court administrator. Example: Lehigh County allows one deferment chosen in the online questionnaire.

list: served on a jury within the last 3 years
close relative of a criminal homicide victim
employee of a small employer not covered by job protection
excuses.text: Only the grounds listed in the statute; ask the county jury office, which decides hardship requests.

penalty.text: Failing to appear is contempt of court: fine up to $500, up to 10 days in jail, or both.

missing: oneDayOneTrial (no statewide rule; set by county)

jurisdictions.name: Rhode Island

pay.text: $25 for each day of attendance at Superior Court (since July 1, 2022); not paid for weekends, holidays or days you are excused. Providence County jurors get free parking and shuttle.

employer.text: No duty to pay wages unless a contract or collective agreement says so; an employer may not take away the job, raises, promotions or benefits. Violation is a misdemeanor.

term.text: Providence and Kent counties: two days or one trial. Washington and Newport counties: usually one day or one trial.

frequency.text: No one serves more than once every three years.

deferral.text: After receiving a summons, log in to Jury Service eResponse and choose 'Apply to defer'; pick a new date on the calendar; the Jury Commissioner approves or denies.

excuses.text: Apply to be excused or disqualified through Jury Service eResponse; the Office of the Jury Commissioner decides. The court asks people to request excuse only for urgent reasons. Statutory grounds (R.I. Gen. Laws § 9-9-3, § 9-10-9) could not be read: legislature site unreachable.

penalty.text: A juror who fails to attend without a satisfactory excuse can be held in contempt and fined at least $20 (no maximum stated in this section).

jurisdictions.name: South Carolina

pay.mileage: Paid; rate varies by county (statute sets 5 cents per mile round trip as the base)
pay.text: Pay is set county by county. The old statute lists per diems of $2 to $10 by county; counties now pay more (e.g. Georgetown County pays $25 a day). Paid whether or not you sit on a case.

employer.text: No state law requires wages during service. An employer who fires or demotes an employee for jury service can be sued for up to one year's wages.

age.text: People 65 or older are exempt if they ask; a phone call to the clerk of court confirming date of birth is enough.

term.text: Circuit court jurors are summoned for a court term beginning a given week; the length is set locally.

frequency.text: Not drawn more than once every three calendar years, and never more than once a calendar year (the court's web page cites two years).

deferral.text: Students and school employees get their service moved outside the school term on request (with proof). Essential workers may be transferred to another term by affidavit. Responses and waiver requests go through the clerk of court or the Juror Web Portal.

list: legal custody of a child under 7 without adequate childcare
primary caretaker of a person 65+ or a severely disabled person
person essential to a business that would have to close
good and sufficient cause shown to the judge
served on a circuit court jury recently
excuses.text: Mark the ground on the summons response form or Juror Web Portal; caretaker and business grounds need a notarized affidavit to the clerk of court.

penalty.text: Not attending without a sufficient excuse: civil penalty up to $100. Violating the excuse rules of § 14-7-860 is a misdemeanor (up to $1,000 and/or 30 days).

missing: pay.dailyRate (set by county; statute figures outdated)

jurisdictions.name: South Dakota

pay.mileage: State mileage rate for each mile actually traveled (UJS lists $0.76 per mile, round trip)
pay.text: $50 for each day you sit on a case; if you are called but not seated, a $10 appearance fee. Paid by the county.

employer.text: The employee keeps job status, pay rate and seniority, but paying wages during the absence is at the employer's discretion. Firing or suspending a juror is a Class 2 misdemeanor.

age.text: People 80 or older may ask to be excused; the judge gives the request substantial weight but can refuse it.

term.text: Each circuit's presiding judge decides how jury panels are used and summoned; your term of service is shown in the UJS Juror Portal.

frequency.text: Anyone who has already served (summoned and appeared for a trial) since the current master list was drawn is skipped; the list is compiled each year.

deferral.text: Enter unavailable dates in the online questionnaire or tell the local clerk of courts; written proof may be requested. Students contact the clerk.

list: breastfeeding a baby under one year
parent of a baby under six weeks or expected during service
other reasons approved by the presiding judge
excuses.text: Send a written request to the clerk of courts; the presiding judge decides. Breastfeeding/new-parent requests go in writing within 10 days of the summons.

penalty.text: Contempt of court: fine of $50 to $500; up to 10 days in county jail if you ignore a second order of attachment.
