jurisdictions.name: Tennessee

pay.text: Each county sets juror pay under Tenn. Code § 22-4-101. The statewide minimum could not be read on an official site. County examples: Blount $10 a day, Knox $11 a day, Hamilton $25 a day.

employer.text: Employers with 5 or more regular employees must pay usual wages for time spent serving and traveling, minus the juror fee. This does not apply to employers with fewer than 5 regular employees or to temporary workers employed under 6 months.
employer.notice: Show the summons to your immediate superior on your next workday after receiving it.

age.text: There is no automatic age exemption. People 75 or older are excused if they file a written declaration that a mental or physical condition makes them unable to serve.

term.text: Set by each county: for example 2 weeks in Knox County and 2 or 3 weeks in Hamilton County.

frequency.text: Hamilton County lists, as an eligibility criterion, not having served on a federal or state jury in the past 24 months. A statewide statute could not be read.

deferral.text: Handled by the county jury coordinator or clerk. Knox: ask at orientation or contact the Jury Coordinator. Hamilton: request at least 10 days ahead and pick a new 2- or 3-week term.

list: undue or extreme physical or financial hardship
caregiver who cannot find a substitute
costs harming necessary daily living expenses
excuses.text: Send the county jury clerk a jury service affidavit with documentation before your date (Hamilton asks for at least 10 days ahead).

penalty.text: Statewide maximum not found in an official source. Knox County says a no-show may be held in contempt and fined $500.

missing: statewide statute text (TN code only on Lexis; tncourts.gov behind a bot check)

pay.text: State minimums: at least $20 for the first day and at least $58 for each later day; each county's commissioners court sets its own amount at or above these. Municipal-court jurors are not covered.

employer.text: No Texas statute requires private employers to pay wages during jury service.
employer.notice: To get the job back after an unlawful firing, the employee must tell the employer as soon as practical after release that they intend to return.

age.text: People 75 or older may claim an exemption, temporary or permanent, by filing a signed statement with the clerk.

frequency.text: Exemption on request if you served as a petit juror in the county in the previous 24 months (counties of 200,000+) or 3 years (counties of 250,000+); none statewide in smaller counties.

deferral.text: Ask the court clerk in person, in writing or by phone before your date. A first postponement is granted automatically (if none in the past year) to a date within 6 months; later ones need an extreme emergency.

list: legal custody of a child under 12 who would be left without adequate supervision
college or university student in attendance
primary caretaker of a person unable to care for themselves
recent jury service in large counties
active-duty military deployed away from home station
physical or mental impairment or inability to comprehend English
any reasonable sworn excuse accepted by the court
excuses.text: Exemptions are claimed by filing a signed statement with the clerk before the date; the judge may also accept any reasonable sworn excuse. Economic excuses need the parties' approval.

penalty.text: Ignoring a summons or giving false exemption information can bring a contempt fine of $100 to $1,000. Section 62.111 also sets a fine of $100 to $500 for jurors who fail to attend without reasonable excuse.

pay.mileage: Per-mile travel allowance at the rate the Administrative Office sets for court staff using private cars, for the shortest route to and from court; tolls paid, parking at the court's discretion
pay.text: $50 a day from day one. A trial juror who sits more than 10 days on one case may get up to $10 more a day ($60) if the judge orders it; grand jurors after 45 days. Federal government employees get their regular salary instead.

employer.text: Federal law does not require private employers to keep paying wages during federal jury service; check the employer's own policy.

age.text: No automatic age exemption in the statute. Most district courts' jury plans let people over 70 ask for a permanent excuse; each of the 94 courts sets its own rule.

term.text: Set by each district court. A trial (petit) juror hears at most one case and is then discharged; nobody can be required to attend more than 30 days as a petit juror in any two-year period, except to finish a case. Grand jurors generally serve up to 18 months (24 with extension).

frequency.text: In any two-year period no one can be required to serve more than 30 days as a petit juror, on more than one grand jury, or as both grand and petit juror; most courts also excuse on request anyone who served on a federal jury in the past two years.

deferral.text: Ask the district court that summoned you, usually through its eJuror page: you can request an excuse or deferral and pick another time to serve if the deferral is granted. Rules vary by court.

list: served on a federal jury within the past two years (most courts, on request)
volunteer firefighter, rescue squad or ambulance crew (most courts, on request)
excuses.text: Temporary excuses or deferrals are granted at the court's discretion for undue hardship or extreme inconvenience; local plans add group excuses on request. Active-duty military, professional fire and police, and full-time public officers are barred (exempt), not excused.

penalty.text: Someone who skips a summons can be ordered to show cause; without good cause, up to $1,000 fine, up to 3 days in jail, community service, or a combination. Employers who punish a juror face up to $5,000 civil penalty per violation.

pay.mileage: $1 for each 4 miles beyond 50 miles, one way
pay.text: $18.50 for the first day and $49 for each later day, set by state law. The court FAQ adds that parking or transit costs may be reimbursed with proof of payment.

employer.text: No wage requirement, but an employer cannot make you use annual, vacation or sick leave for jury service.

age.text: Utah has no age exemption: no qualified prospective juror is exempt. An older person may still ask to be excused for undue hardship or incapacity.

term.text: One day or one trial. Your qualification term runs 1 month (Salt Lake County district courts), 3 months (Davis, Utah, Weber) or 6 months elsewhere.

frequency.text: After you attend court, you cannot be summoned again for at least two years.

deferral.text: The court may postpone service if you show good cause; contact the court using the number on your notice.

excuses.text: Ask the court and support the request with an affidavit, sworn testimony or other evidence. The excuse lasts as long as the reason exists.

penalty.text: Failing to appear or to complete service is contempt of court: up to a $1,000 fine, 30 days in jail, or both ($500 and 5 days before a justice court judge or commissioner).

pay.text: $50 per day of attendance, meant to cover travel and other expenses; no separate mileage rate in the statute. Paid for only one case per day.

employer.text: No duty to pay wages, but the employer cannot force the employee to use sick leave or vacation; after 4+ hours of jury duty the employee cannot be required to start a shift beginning at/after 5 p.m. that day or before 3 a.m. the next day.
employer.notice: Employee must give reasonable notice of the summons to the employer

age.text: Anyone over 73 (i.e. 74 or older) may ask to be exempted.

term.text: One term of court, which can last up to four months depending on the circuit; the summons gives the dates.

frequency.text: Anyone who reported for jury duty in a state court in the previous three years is left off the next jury list.

deferral.text: Call the number on the summons; the judge may defer service for genuine hardship, or defer it to the next term for an occupational inconvenience (incl. full-time students and parents of children 16 or younger).

list: custody of a child 16 or younger needing continuous care
custody of a child under 18 with a serious health condition
caregiver of a person with a serious health condition
spouse summoned to the same panel
sole essential worker of a business or farm
sole essential firefighter of a locality
disability substantially impairing ability to serve
excuses.text: These groups may serve but are exempt on request; certain officials (lawyers, judges, police, etc.) are exempt outright. Contact the court on the summons.

penalty.text: A juror who fails to appear without sufficient excuse is fined $50 to $200; the court may also treat it as contempt.

pay.mileage: On request and on a showing of hardship, travel from home to court and back at the state-employee rate
pay.text: Superior Court jurors get $30 a day on request, unless their employer already paid them.

employer.text: No wage requirement. The employee keeps seniority, fringe benefits and vacation credit while serving.

age.text: There is no age exemption: no one is excused automatically. The judge may excuse a person who asks and shows undue hardship.

term.text: Two-year term: during it you can be called to jury selection at most 3 times and to serve on a trial date at most 3 times.

frequency.text: Your name can be put on a venire for a state court only once in any two-year period.

deferral.text: On an individual request showing undue hardship, the judge may excuse you for part of the two-year term, which works as a postponement. The court's own procedure (online questionnaire, Jury Administration) could not be read.

list: undue hardship on the prospective juror
not capable because of mental or physical condition
excuses.text: Nobody is excused automatically. Make an individual request to the presiding judge showing undue hardship. People not physically or mentally able to serve are not qualified.

penalty.text: A summoned juror who doesn't appear and gives no satisfactory excuse faces a civil penalty of up to $200, which can be waived for good cause. Ignoring a questionnaire order can be contempt.

pay.mileage: Mileage at the state rate set under RCW 43.03.060, each day of attendance
pay.text: Each county sets a uniform daily fee between $10 and $25; most counties pay $10. Mileage is paid on top.

employer.text: Employers must grant leave but are not required to pay wages during jury service.

age.text: People 80 or older who attest they cannot serve for health reasons must be excused on request; no doctor's note required.

term.text: Each court sets its own jury terms; state policy says a term should ideally be one week or less and service one day or one trial, whichever is longer.

frequency.text: If summoned again within 12 months, a juror who already served at least one week in that period may ask in writing to be excused.

deferral.text: Call or write to the number/address on the summons to reschedule; an excused juror may be reassigned to another term within 12 months.

list: any reason the court deems sufficient
excuses.text: Ask the court named on the summons. A breastfeeding exemption (infant under 24 months) is added to RCW 2.36.100 from January 1, 2027.

penalty.text: Intentionally failing to appear is a misdemeanor, punishable by up to 90 days in jail and/or a $1,000 fine (general misdemeanor penalty, RCW 9.92.030).

jurisdictions.name: Wisconsin

pay.mileage: State mileage rate (s. 20.916(8)) for each mile traveled each day, round trip
pay.text: Statutory minimum is $16 per day; each county board sets the actual rate (may pay by half-day, and may set a different first-day amount in one-day/one-trial circuits).

employer.text: Employers must grant leave with no loss of seniority or pay advancement, but the statute does not require wages to be paid.

age.text: No age exemption: Wisconsin abolished exemptions and bars excluding qualified jurors because of age; only an individual excuse or deferral is possible.

term.text: Circuits may opt for one day or one trial. Elsewhere, availability is capped at 31 consecutive days and at most 5 days in court unless a trial needs more.

frequency.text: Once in any 4-year period in counties without one day/one trial; in one day/one trial circuits the protected period is set by the judges at 2 to 4 years.

deferral.text: Ask the court (or the clerk of circuit court, if authorized) named on the summons; it may move your service to a later date it sets. Documentation may be required.

list: cannot fulfill the responsibilities of a juror
excuses.text: No automatic exemptions. The court may excuse someone who cannot fulfill a juror's responsibilities; hardship normally leads to a deferral. The clerk may be authorized to decide.

penalty.text: Failing to attend without being excused is contempt of court; after a show-cause hearing the circuit court may impose a sanction of up to $500.

jurisdictions.caveat: Some texts cited on this page were read in archived copies (web.archive.org, 2025 and 2026) of the official pages linked, because the official site refused our connection on October 29, 2026.

pay.mileage: Round-trip mileage at the rate set by the Secretary of Administration, each day of required attendance
pay.text: The statute lets each circuit court set the daily reimbursement between $15 and $40; the state court system says jurors receive $40 a day plus mileage. Paid by the State Treasury.

employer.text: Employers must excuse the employee for the days of service but need not pay wages; they may not cut pay for time the employee was not actually away.
employer.notice: Employee must show the summons to the immediate supervisor on the next working day after receiving it

age.text: People 70 or older are qualified but must be excused if they ask (box on the qualification questionnaire).

term.text: Service is for a term of court; within any two years no one may be required to attend more than 30 court days (unless needed to finish a case) or serve as a petit juror at more than one term. Call-in system means not every day in person.

frequency.text: Anyone who attended and was paid as a petit, grand or magistrate juror in the previous two years is disqualified.

deferral.text: Write to the presiding circuit judge; the court may excuse you for a set period, after which you must report again as directed.

list: current National Guard or reserves member
substantial physical or mental disability (disqualification, physician's certificate may be required)
excuses.text: No occupation is automatically exempt. Put the request in writing to the presiding circuit judge.

penalty.text: A no-show is ordered to show cause; without good cause it is civil contempt with a fine up to $1,000.

pay.mileage: Paid when the one-way trip from home to court is over 5 miles, at the state travel rate (capped at the IRS nontaxable rate, W.S. 9-3-103)
pay.text: $30 for each full or part day. After more than 5 consecutive days (weekends and holidays not counted), the court may add $20 a day, for $50.

employer.text: The Wyoming jury statutes protect the job but contain no rule requiring employers to keep paying wages.

age.text: Anyone aged 72 or older may ask to be excused; it is not automatic.

term.text: Each court sets its own jury term; jurors are summoned for that term. Example: Teton County District Court uses six-month terms.

frequency.text: After serving on a jury you are, on request, excused for the rest of that jury term and the rest of the calendar year; the court may also excuse you for the following term.

deferral.text: No statewide postponement rule found in the statute; courts handle it. Example: Teton County lets jurors ask in advance to be excused from trial dates in certain periods (full-time students away at school until a break).

list: threatened material injury or destruction of property
sickness or death of a family member
already served during the jury term
excuses.text: Hardship or business inconvenience alone is not enough. Exempt (on sworn declaration): salaried firefighters, police, elected officials, active-duty National Guard and military where federal law exempts them.

penalty.text: A juror who wilfully skips without reasonable excuse can be arrested, brought to court and held in contempt; the jury statute sets no fine amount. Employers who punish a juror owe up to $1,000 exemplary damages per violation.
